title: Localization triangle for the exceptional inverse image
statement:
Let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, and assume that $j$ is quasi-compact [def-pur-flasque-support, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. Work with all module sheaves over the constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], without a constructibility condition. Let $K$ be a bounded below complex, or its object in $D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $s^!M=s^{-1}\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ as in [def-pur-flasque-support], and let $Rs^!$ be its right derived functor on $D^+$, computed on bounded below complexes of injectives [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective].

The injective-resolution and cone construction of [def-pur-support-triangle] gives a distinguished triangle
$$
 s_*Rs^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
 \longrightarrow (s_*Rs^!K)[1]
$$
in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. Here $s_*$ is exact and denotes also its termwise induced derived functor. The functor $Rs^!$ is right adjoint to this $s_*$ on the bounded below derived categories. Consequently any exceptional inverse image defined as a right adjoint to this same $s_*$ on these same categories is naturally identified with $Rs^!$, compatibly with the counit. The triangle is independent of the chosen injective resolution under the derived comparison maps, is functorial in $K$, and is compatible with etale base change in precisely the sense of [def-pur-triangle-meaning, def-weil-etale-morphism].

proof.text: Use the compatible small sites and module universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each of $T=X,Z,U$, the category $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_T)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], and has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. The general abelian-category statement [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] therefore supplies a bounded below complex $I$ of injectives representing $K$; it is K-injective. This uses that node's general first clause, not its example restricted to the etale site. For an input complex $K$, the inverse of the chosen isomorphism $QI\cong QK$ is represented by a chain map $r:K\to I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Its derived image is invertible, so its maps on all cohomology objects are isomorphisms; hence $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism and supplies the actual resolution arrow required by [def-pur-support-triangle]. For an input derived object choose a bounded below representative first. All sheaf functors used below are additive; applying one termwise preserves a lower bound. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], the right derived functor of $s^!$ exists and its value on $K$ is represented by $s^!I$. For the actual bounded below input complex, Lean uses Mathlib CochainComplex.Plus.modelCategoryQuillen.exists_quasiIso_injective directly: it supplies a quasi-isomorphism K → I with injective terms and the same strict lower bound. Thus this auxiliary resolution-arrow clause needs no lift of an abstract derived isomorphism.

Put $G_ZM=\ker(\eta_{j,M})$. The stated natural comparison in [def-pur-flasque-support] is $q_M:G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^!M$, since $j$ is quasi-compact. The module operations of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] give the open and closed inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions. For a sheaf $N$ on $Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $j^*s_*N=0$, so the adjunct of any composite $s_*N\to M\to j_*j^*M$ is zero. Thus every map $s_*N\to M$ factors uniquely through $G_ZM$. Using $q_M$ and full faithfulness of $s_*$ from [lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful] gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(s_*N,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(s_*N,G_ZM)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(s_*N,s_*s^!M)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(N,s^!M).$$
This proves $s_*\dashv s^!$. Its counit is exactly the inclusion $G_ZM\hookrightarrow M$ after $q_M^{-1}$, so the first arrow is specified, rather than a freely chosen map.

source.place: Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero); explicit kernel factorization of blueprint proof, second paragraph

proof.text:
The exactness of $s_*$ on these finite constant-coefficient module sheaves follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with its quasi-compact-complement hypothesis satisfied. Hence $s^!$ preserves injectives: for a monomorphism $N\hookrightarrow N'$ on $Z$, an arrow $N\to s^!J$ transposes to $s_*N\to J$; exactness makes $s_*N\hookrightarrow s_*N'$ monic, so injectivity of $J$ extends the arrow, and transposition gives the extension on $Z$. Consequently $s^!I$ is bounded below with injective terms and is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. The termwise adjunction descends to homotopy categories by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. For any bounded below representative $L$ on $Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(s_*L,K)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A_X)}(s_*L,I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A_Z)}(L,s^!I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z)}(L,Rs^!K).$$
Exactness of $s_*$ ensures that its termwise value represents its derived value [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. These natural bijections prove the derived adjunction, with the counit from step 2. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to any other right adjoint on these same categories to obtain the claimed counit-compatible identification. No identification with a transported functor on a different category is inferred. Lean uses the existing Adjunction.derivedPlus construction and its unit/counit equations, proving the normalized model identities through the fixed bounded/unbounded derived-functor comparisons.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); explicit derived Hom adjunction; blueprint proof, second paragraph

proof.text: For the open immersion $j$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] states that restriction is exact and preserves injectives, and [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies it with restriction to the localized site, including the constant coefficients. Thus $j^*I$ is a bounded below complex of injectives representing $j^*K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] its direct image $j_*j^*I$ represents $Rj_*j^*K$. The natural map $I\to j_*j^*I$ is termwise the open adjunction unit of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so its derived class is the specified restriction map. This computation also agrees with the unbounded $Rj_*$ fixed in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: its chosen K-injective model and $j^*I$ represent the same derived object. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] the identity and its inverse lift to mutually inverse homotopy classes of chain maps between those models. The additive termwise $j_*$ preserves their inverse homotopies, so their images are canonically isomorphic in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. The comparison carries the derived unit to the displayed unit by naturality.

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, and its exact extension-by-zero argument; derived.tex Tag 05TI, lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-support-exact] to $I$, the finite commutative ring $\Lambda$, and the given quasi-compact complementary $j$. It gives the actual short exact sequence of complexes $0\to A=s_*s^!I\xrightarrow{u}B=I\xrightarrow{\eta_j}C=j_*j^*I\to0$, with its first arrow the inverse-comparison inclusion of step 2. Use the cone and differential of [def-pur-support-triangle]. By [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], the specified map $q:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to C$, $q(b,a)=\eta_j(b)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. The derived-category structure in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $Q(q)$ invertible and makes the image of the cone triangle $A\to B\to\operatorname{Cone}(u)\xrightarrow{-p}A[1]$ distinguished. Identify its third term with $C$ by $Q(q)$. The resulting second arrow is the restriction map, because $q\circ i=\eta_j$, and the boundary is $\delta=-Q(p)\circ Q(q)^{-1}$, with the shift identification understood. This constructs the specified distinguished triangle. Steps 1, 3 and 4 identify its terms with $s_*Rs^!K,K,Rj_*j^*K$. In Lean, shortExact_sectionsWithSupport supplies arrows characterized by their composites with the canonical supported comparison. Cancel that comparison, which is invertible, to identify the supplied first arrow with supportModelInclusion; identify the second arrow degreewise from its unit equation. Mathlib triangleOfSES_distinguished then applies definitionally to the specified cone quotient and signed boundary.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, including the preceding explicit construction q and the cone triangle; blueprint proof, first paragraph

proof.text:
For a derived morphism $K\to K'$, choose injective models $I,I'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] it is represented by a unique homotopy class of chain maps $f:I\to I'$. Naturality of the support kernel in [def-pur-flasque-support] and the unit in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] makes $(a,b,c)=(s_*s^!f,f,j_*j^*f)$ a map of the short exact sequences in step 5. The cone formula of [def-pur-support-triangle] gives a chain map $t:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to\operatorname{Cone}(u')$, $t(b_0,a_0)=(b(b_0),a(a_0))$. Direct substitution in the differential gives $q't=cq$ and $p't=a[1]p$. Since both $Q(q)$ and $Q(q')$ are invertible by [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], these equations give
$$a[1]\delta=-a[1]p q^{-1}=-p'tq^{-1}=-p'(q')^{-1}c=\delta'c$$
in the derived category. Thus $(a,b,c)$ is a map of the specified triangles, including the fourth square. If $f-g=dh+hd$, applying any of the three additive functors gives $F(f)-F(g)=dF(h)+F(h)d$; the three components consequently have the same derived classes. Hence the triangle map depends only on the derived morphism. Identities and composites are represented by identity chain maps and composites, proving the functor laws. For two resolutions of the same $K$, the unique homotopy class representing the identity is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Each additive functor preserves that inverse and its homotopies, so the comparison is an isomorphism of triangles. Three resolutions satisfy the comparison cocycle because the composite represents the same identity. This proves the canonicality and functoriality of [def-pur-triangle-meaning].

source.place: Tags 070I, lemma-K-injective, and 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; explicit homotopy and comparison calculation for blueprint proof, third paragraph

proof.text:
Let $v:X'\to X$ be etale and form the closed/open pair $s':Z'\to X'$, $j':U'\to X'$. By [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison] the map $v$ is weakly etale, so [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies its constant-coefficient inverse image with restriction to the slice at $X'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives], $v^*I$ is a bounded below injective model of $v^*K$. The morphism $j'$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], so [lem-pur-support-exact] applies also to the primed pair. For an object $V\to X'$ of the pro-etale site, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] gives
$$(v^*j_*j^*I)(V)=I(V\times_XU)=(j'_*j'^*v^*I)(V).$$
These equalities use the fibre-product identification $V\times_{X'}U'=V\times_XU$ and commute with every restriction map and coefficient action. Both open units send a section to its restriction along this same fibre product. Exactness of $v^*$ from [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] therefore identifies the kernel of one unit with the kernel of the other. The natural support comparisons of [def-pur-flasque-support], valid for both quasi-compact complements, identify the first terms too. We have obtained an isomorphism between the pulled-back short exact sequence of step 5 and the short exact sequence for $v^*I$, with all three maps specified. Lean verifies the unit compatibility directly from the canonical mate identity and conjugacy of upperStarComp with lowerStarComp. The first component is the unique induced kernel isomorphism; no arbitrary comparison is chosen.

source.place: Tags 09A5, section-morphism (direct image by fibre-product evaluation), 09BN, lemma-open-immersion, and 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08FI; explicit localized-site calculation

proof.text: The exact inverse image $v^*$ induces a triangulated functor by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. It commutes with the specified cone of [def-pur-support-triangle]: in degree $m$, the identification is $v^*(B^m\oplus A^{m+1})=v^*B^m\oplus v^*A^{m+1}$, and additivity carries $d(b,a)=(d_Bb+u(a),-d_Aa)$ to the identical primed matrix. Under step 7's identification of the quotient, the cone map is still $q(b,a)=\eta_j(b)$ and the projection $p$ is the same shifted projection. Consequently, for the canonical boundary constructed in step 5, with $q$ inverted by [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso], applying $v^*$ sends $-p\circ q^{-1}$ to $-p'\circ(q')^{-1}$, using that a functor preserves inverses of isomorphisms. Thus the fourth square commutes as well as the first two. Finally step 6 compares the model $v^*I$ with any chosen injective model on $X'$. This proves the full triangle comparison, including its boundary, required by [def-pur-triangle-meaning]. Lean uses DerivedCategory.map_triangleOfSESδ and triangleOfSES.map, whose explicit formula is definitionally the specified quotient inverse and signed projection.
